quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Auxiliary 'do/does' agreement follows the true subject, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: ___ your colleague who joined last month need any help with onboarding?
quests.completedSentence: Does your colleague who joined last month need any help with onboarding?
quests.grammarRule: Auxiliary 'do/does' agreement follows the true subject, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Your colleague' is singular, even with 'who joined last month' in between. The question needs 'does'.
quests.nativeTip: Look past the description of when your colleague joined to find the true subject.
quests.example: Does your colleague who joined last month need any help with onboarding?

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Auxiliary 'do/does' agreement follows the true subject, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: ___ the students who missed the lecture need to catch up on notes?
quests.completedSentence: Do the students who missed the lecture need to catch up on notes?
quests.grammarRule: Auxiliary 'do/does' agreement follows the true subject, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The students' is plural, so the question needs 'do'.
quests.nativeTip: The clause about missing the lecture doesn't change how many students there are.
quests.example: Do the students who missed the lecture need to catch up on notes?

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: Auxiliary 'do/does' agreement follows the true subject, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The report ___ not include the data from last quarter.
quests.completedSentence: The report does not include the data from last quarter.
quests.grammarRule: Auxiliary 'do/does' agreement follows the true subject, even with an interrupting phrase
quests.ruleExplanation: 'The report' is singular, so the negative form uses 'does': 'does not include'.
quests.nativeTip: Consider how many documents 'the report' names, then think about which negative form fits.
quests.example: The report does not include the data from last quarter.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: The main verb stays in its base form after 'did' / 'didn't', regardless of the subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Did the landlord ___ the request yesterday?
quests.completedSentence: Did the landlord approve the request yesterday?
quests.grammarRule: The main verb stays in its base form after 'did' / 'didn't', regardless of the subject
quests.ruleExplanation: After 'did', the main verb always stays in its base form, so 'approve' is correct, not 'approves'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Did' already shows the question is in the past - the main verb doesn't need its own ending.
quests.example: Did the landlord approve the request yesterday?

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: The main verb stays in its base form after 'did' / 'didn't', regardless of the subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: Did the students ___ their homework before class?
quests.completedSentence: Did the students finish their homework before class?
quests.grammarRule: The main verb stays in its base form after 'did' / 'didn't', regardless of the subject
quests.ruleExplanation: After 'did', the main verb stays in its base form: 'finish', not 'finishes'.
quests.nativeTip: Even with a plural subject, the verb after 'did' still doesn't take an ending.
quests.example: Did the students finish their homework before class?

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: The main verb stays in its base form after 'did' / 'didn't', regardless of the subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: The team didn't ___ enough time to prepare.

quests.grammarRule: The main verb stays in its base form after 'did' / 'didn't', regardless of the subject
quests.ruleExplanation: After 'didn't', the main verb stays in its base form: 'have', not 'has'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Didn't' already carries the negative and the past tense - the main verb stays plain.

quests.conceptTitle: Grammar Scale: The verb after 'can/could' always stays in its base form, regardless of the subject
quests.sentenceWithBlank: She can ___ five languages fluently.

quests.ruleExplanation: After 'can', the main verb always stays in its base form: 'speak', not 'speaks' - this is true no matter who the subject is.
quests.nativeTip: Modals like 'can' never add -s, and neither does the verb that follows them.
quests.example: She can speak five languages fluently.
